extraction.name: FOMO60K
extraction.description: A large-scale, heterogeneous dataset of 60,529 brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources. The dataset includes both clinical- and research-grade images, multiple MRI sequences, and a wide range of anatomical and pathological variability, including scans with large brain anomalies.
extraction.creator: Asbjørn Munk, Stefano Cerri, Jakob Ambsdorf, Julia Machnio, Sebastian Nørgaard Llambias, Vardan Nersesjan, Christian Hedeager Krag, Peirong Liu, Pablo Rocamora García, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi, Mikael Boesen, Michael Eriksen Benros, Juan Eugenio Iglesias, Mads Nielsen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: FOMO60K is derived from 16 publicly available datasets, aggregated to create a large-scale heterogeneous brain MRI dataset. The dataset spans both clinical- and research-grade imaging, includes multiple MRI sequences, and captures anatomical and pathological diversity, including scans with large brain anomalies.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 60,529 brain MRI scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources: MGH Wild, SOOP, BraTS-GEN, OASIS1, OASIS2, MSD Braintumor, IXI, NIMH, DLBS, IDEAS, ARC, MBSR, UCLA, QTAB, NKI, and AOMIC ID1000.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MRI preprocessing comprised three main steps: reorienting images to RAS (Right–Anterior–Superior) orientation, affine co-registration, and skull-stripping. All scans were first reoriented to RAS and affinely co-registered using the mri_coreg command from FreeSurfer 7.4.1, with default parameters. Within each MRI session, scans were aligned to the image with the highest spatial resolution to preserve anatomical detail. For diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) scans stored in 4D format, if a b=0 (non-diffusion-weighted) volume was available, it was extracted and saved separately. For the b=1000 shell, three diffusion-weighted volumes were selected based on their gradient directions being most closely aligned with the canonical x, y, and z axes. The corresponding volumes were averaged to produce a single representative 3D image. Skull-stripping was performed using SynthSeg (FreeSurfer 7.4.1), which outputs segmentation masks of brain structures. Skull-stripping was only applied when the images were not already defaced or skull-stripped by the dataset provider, or when visual inspection identified residual cranial features that could compromise anonymization. Minimal preprocessing was applied to retain the raw characteristics of the original images while improving usability.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will continue to grow in future releases as additional cohorts and modalities become available.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: FOMO60K is intended to support the development and benchmarking of self-supervised learning methods in medical imaging at scale. The dataset can be used with no further pre-processing for pre-training. FOMO60K was developed in parallel with the FOMO25 challenge at MICCAI 2025, which aims to catalyze progress in self-supervised learning for medical imaging.
